\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অনুষ্ঠান} (ônushṭhān)}{অনুষ্ঠান (ônushṭhān)}]{\bn{অনুষ্ঠান} (ônushṭhān) — a ceremony; a function}

\label{lesson:BN-C312-onushthan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to go round, then the Bengali for packed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অনুষ্ঠান}}
\textbf{\bn{অনুষ্ঠান}} — \emph{ônushṭhān} — \textquotedblleft{}a ceremony; a function\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়ের} \bn{অনুষ্ঠান} \bn{সন্ধ্যায়} \bn{শুরু} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{biyer ônushṭhān sôndhyāy shuru hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The wedding ceremony began in the evening.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অনুষ্ঠান}} (\emph{ônushṭhān}) is Sanskrit \emph{anuṣṭhāna}, 'carrying out, performance' (Monier-Williams), as of a rite; today it is any ceremony or programme.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônushṭhān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônushṭhān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biyer ônushṭhān sôndhyāy shuru hôlô.} — The wedding ceremony began in the evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to go round, then the Bengali for packed, then say \emph{ônushṭhān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অনুষ্ঠান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A ceremony; a function\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মালা} (mālā)}{মালা (mālā)}]{\bn{মালা} (mālā) — a garland}

\label{lesson:BN-C312-mala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for packed, then the Bengali for a ceremony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মালা}}
\textbf{\bn{মালা}} — \emph{mālā} — \textquotedblleft{}a garland\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়েতে} \bn{বর} \bn{আর} \bn{কনে} \bn{ফুলের} \bn{মালা} \bn{পরল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{biyete bôr ār kône phuler mālā pôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the wedding the bride and groom wore flower garlands.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মালা}} (\emph{mālā}) is Sanskrit \emph{mālā}, 'a wreath, a garland; a string of beads' (Monier-Williams), unchanged.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mālā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mālā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biyete bôr ār kône phuler mālā pôrlô.} — At the wedding the bride and groom wore flower garlands.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for packed, then the Bengali for a ceremony, then say \emph{mālā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মালা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A garland\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সানাই} (sānāi)}{সানাই (sānāi)}]{\bn{সানাই} (sānāi) — a shehnai (a wedding pipe)}

\label{lesson:BN-C312-sanai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a ceremony, then the Bengali for a garland.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সানাই}}
\textbf{\bn{সানাই}} — \emph{sānāi} — \textquotedblleft{}a shehnai (a wedding pipe)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়েতে} \bn{একটা} \bn{লোক} \bn{সারাদিন} \bn{সানাই} \bn{বাজাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{biyete ekṭā lok sārādin sānāi bājālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the wedding a man played the shehnai all day.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সানাই}} (\emph{sānāi}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{shahnāī}, 'the king's pipe'; its reedy sound means a wedding in Bengal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sānāi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sānāi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biyete ekṭā lok sārādin sānāi bājālô.} — At the wedding a man played the shehnai all day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a ceremony, then the Bengali for a garland, then say \emph{sānāi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সানাই} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A shehnai (a wedding pipe)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উলু} (ulu)}{উলু (ulu)}]{\bn{উলু} (ulu) — ululation (the women's festive cry)}

\label{lesson:BN-C312-ulu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a garland, then the Bengali for a shehnai.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উলু}}
\textbf{\bn{উলু}} — \emph{ulu} — \textquotedblleft{}ululation (the women's festive cry)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বর} \bn{এলে} \bn{মহিলারা} \bn{উলু} \bn{দেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bôr ele môhilārā ulu den.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the groom arrives, the women give the festive cry.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উলু}} (\emph{ulu}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{ululi}, 'crying aloud' (CDIAL 2358, which lists Bengali \emph{ulu}, the sound women make at festivals). \bn{উলু} \bn{দেওয়া}, to give the cry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ulu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ulu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôr ele môhilārā ulu den.} — When the groom arrives, the women give the festive cry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a garland, then the Bengali for a shehnai, then say \emph{ulu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উলু} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ululation (the women's festive cry)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বরযাত্রী} (bôrjātrī)}{বরযাত্রী (bôrjātrī)}]{\bn{বরযাত্রী} (bôrjātrī) — the groom's wedding party}

\label{lesson:BN-C312-borjatri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a shehnai, then the Bengali for ululation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বরযাত্রী}}
\textbf{\bn{বরযাত্রী}} — \emph{bôrjātrī} — \textquotedblleft{}the groom's wedding party\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বরযাত্রীরা} \bn{রাত} \bn{আটটায়} \bn{পৌঁছাল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bôrjātrīrā rāt āṭṭāy poũchhālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The groom's party arrived at eight at night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বরযাত্রী}} (\emph{bôrjātrī}) joins \textbf{\bn{বর}}, the bridegroom, to \textbf{\bn{যাত্রী}}, a traveller — Sanskrit \emph{yātrin}, 'being in a procession' (Monier-Williams): those who travel with the groom to the bride's house.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôrjātrī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôrjātrī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôrjātrīrā rāt āṭṭāy poũchhālô.} — The groom's party arrived at eight at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a shehnai, then the Bengali for ululation, then say \emph{bôrjātrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বরযাত্রী} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The groom's wedding party\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
